proof:
# Exact available curves for the strengthened equal-endpoint edge credit

Let A,K,B be d-dimensional convex bodies, d>=1, with |A|=|B|=v>0 and
M=(A+B)/2 subset K. Place them at bases -1,0,1. Write

    Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, t=|K|/v, r=|M|/v, 1<=r<=t.

The bounded question is whether the actual maximum RAW mixed depth is
always at least (3/4)Gamma(t+1)v for 1<=t<=3. This note proves the
available exact bound curve, records subclasses where that target is
proved, and certifies a gap in the existing bound bundle. It neither
asserts this strengthened target in the remaining regime nor supplies
an actual-body counterexample to it.

Subsequent status: the full strengthened equal-endpoint target is now
proved at the true mixed centroid for all d>=1 in
`candidate 660db01ed45063dd`,
using dominated midpoint coupling and a new mass-dependent centroid
dual. The gap below remains a certified limitation of the three
specific earlier source bounds, not an unresolved target theorem.

## 1. Three actual middle points and their exact guaranteed budgets

Define, for s>=1,

    R_d(s)=[1-(2[(1-Gamma)s]^(1/d)-1)^d]_+.

The quantity inside the d-th power is nonnegative in this domain.
The three actual candidate points are

    c=(g_A+g_B)/2, g_K, g_M.

They all belong to K. Their raw lower bounds are respectively

    D(c)/v >= 2Gamma,                                      (1)
    D(g_K)/v >= Gamma t+R_d(t),                            (2)
    D(g_M)/v >= Gamma r+R_d(r).                            (3)

Equation (1) is the archived additive-midpoint certificate: the
Minkowski midpoint of the positive centroid caps in A and B pays at
least Gamma v inside K, and every ambient cap through c contains at
least one endpoint centroid, paying a further Gamma v. These are
disjoint integer fibers.

For (2), fix a nonzero continuous normal and a cap through g_K. If the
sum P of its two endpoint cap volumes is at least v, the asserted
endpoint payment follows because R_d<=1. Otherwise both endpoint
residuals have positive volume. Their Minkowski midpoint lies in the
opposite K halfspace through g_K, of volume at most (1-Gamma)|K|.
Brunn--Minkowski and the minimum root sum at fixed residual total give

    v^(1/d)+(v-P)^(1/d)
      <=(v-U)^(1/d)+(v-V)^(1/d)
      <=2[(1-Gamma)|K|]^(1/d),  U+V=P.

Rearrangement gives P>=v R_d(t). The own cap pays Gamma|K|, proving
(2). Equation (3) is the same argument using M, retaining its ordinary
centroid cap inside K. All continuous boundaries have zero d-volume;
full or empty endpoint traces are covered by the preceding alternative.

For pure integer normals, every closed through-middle halfspace
contains K and one full endpoint, with mass (t+1)v, which dominates
these displayed budgets. A containing halfspace can be shifted to
the source before applying the calculations.

## 2. Adding the existing directional width budget

For d>=2 put

    Z_d(r)=2^d r-2,
    L_d(r)=(Z_d(r)+sqrt(Z_d(r)^2-4))/2,
    W_d(r)=(L_d(r)+1)^d /
       [(d+1)^d (L_d(r)^(d/(d-1))+1)^(d-1)].

These are real and positive because Z_d(r)>=2. The archived support
homothety and section-addition arguments give an endpoint payment
P/v>=W_d(r) at g_M. Specifically, the actual width ratio R satisfies
R+1/R<=Z_d(r), and its payment is at least

    (R+1)^d/[(d+1)^d(R^(d/(d-1))+1)^(d-1)].

This expression is symmetric under R->1/R and decreases on R>=1:
its logarithmic derivative has the sign of 1-R^(1/(d-1)). Therefore
substitution of the largest allowed ratio L_d(r) is valid.

The exact three-candidate guaranteed curve is thus

    B_d(t,r)=max{2Gamma, Gamma t+R_d(t),
                    Gamma r+max(R_d(r),W_d(r))},          (4)
    max_(x in K) D(x)>=v B_d(t,r).

The source is selected deterministically by comparing these three
proved numbers, resolving ties in the displayed order. There is no
averaging of candidate points.

If only t is retained, a valid dimension-dependent curve is

    B_d^*(t)=max{2Gamma, Gamma t+R_d(t),
          min_(1<=s<=t)[Gamma s+max(R_d(s),W_d(s))]}.      (5)

The minimum is attained because its scalar function is continuous on
the compact interval [1,t]. This is an explicit one-variable formula,
not a claim that the associated geometric extremizer exists or that
the bound is sharp.

## 3. Ranges and subclasses where the proposed edge credit follows

For every d>=1, (1) proves the requested
(3/4)Gamma(t+1)v whenever 1<=t<=5/3. For t>=3, the own ordinary
centroid bound Gamma t v proves it. These elementary ranges do not
settle 5/3<t<3.

In d=2 the audited uniform g_M budget (308/345)v from
`candidate 59cc2a7b6dcd2dbc`
extends the lower range to

    1<=t<=193/115,

since the target is (t+1)v/3 and 3(308/345)-1=193/115.

If the equal-volume endpoints are translates of one common body, the
entire requested range 1<=t<=3 is proved. Use the permitted affine
shear to align both endpoint copies. Their common centroid belongs to
their midpoint copy inside K. That copy pays Gamma v, and the proved
paired-centroid-tail theorem pays 2Gamma v from the two endpoints,
for every nonvertical cap at that same point. Pure integer caps pay
at least 2v>=3Gamma v. Thus raw depth is at least 3Gamma v, which is
at least the requested target when t<=3. Equal-volume homothetic
endpoints are translates, so they are included without a condition
on the middle shape.

For d=1 this applies to every equal-length endpoint pair. More sharply,
the archived exact asymmetric-three-interval theorem gives, after
optimizing over placements at fixed t in [1,3],

    max raw depth >= (t+5)v/4,                            (6)

with equality when the middle interval extends entirely to one side
of the aligned endpoint interval. It exceeds the requested interval
target 3(t+1)v/8 by (7-t)v/8. Thus any failure of the new edge credit
must have d>=2 and genuinely different endpoint shapes.

## 4. An exact realized gap in this bound bundle

In d=3 let the centered boxes A,B have side lengths

    A: (1,9/4,4/9),   B: (1,4/9,9/4).

Their volumes are v=1. Their actual midpoint is a centered box of volume
r=9409/5184. Let K=(2/r)^(1/3)M, so t=2 and M subset K. This is an
actual positive-volume three-fiber body.

With Gamma_3=27/64, one has

    (1-Gamma_3)r=348133/331776>1,
    (1-Gamma_3)t=37/32>1.

Thus both residual payments R_3(r),R_3(t) vanish. In the first-coordinate
direction the TRUE widths of A,B are equal, so even retaining these
exact widths gives only 1/32 from the support-homothety estimate. Its
g_M budget is

    Gamma_3 r+1/32=9793/12288 < 27/32=2Gamma_3.

The eliminated-width expression W_3(r) is no larger, since the width
function is maximized at ratio one. Consequently (4) is exactly
2Gamma_3=27/32 on these scalar data. The requested target is

    (3/4)Gamma_3(t+1)=243/256,
    243/256-27/32=27/256>0.                              (7)

This proves only that the three displayed lower-bound mechanisms do
not imply the desired curve. The actual body is not a counterexample:
K is centrally symmetric with volume2, so its own center alone has
raw depth at least1>243/256. The missing information in (4) is real
section shape, not an unaccounted fiber or an invalid center.

A supplementary numerical falsification screen of A=T, B=L T,
|det L|=1, K=(A+B)/2 in the plane found no violating finite positive
three-normal cap cover. It is recorded only in the script
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/screen_equal_triangle_endpoint_three_cap_credit_two_sided.py`; no
theorem or gap closure in this note depends on that screen.
